items.title: Leslie Gourse interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996
items.q: They loved Rushing and Rushing was a real blues singer, and he had a higher, plaintive voice. And Joe was not the same type of blues singer.

ctx.x: Well speaking about, “Why can’t you be like Nat Cole,” I read a few things about when Joe had to replace, when Joe became Basie’s singer, he had to follow Jimmy Rushing, and apparently there was some problems with that I guess, maybe over in England or something.

Yes, there were. Well they wanted the same old thing. They loved Rushing and Rushing was a real blues singer, and he had a higher, plaintive voice. And Joe was not the same type of blues singer. He was more polished as a singer. And he had a different gift. And in England they love trad jazz, traditional jazz. And in France too, they had a lot of clubs, and they still have any number of people who only like traditional jazz, trad jazz, early jazz. They still haven’t gotten anywhere near bebop. I don’t even know…
How has the jazz scene changed in New York?
